tagline: The first and only FDA-approved neurostimulator for obstructive sleep apnea.
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue is the primary indicator of growth and technology adoption for Inspire Medical Systems. It directly reflects the success of their commercial strategy and market penetration.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total amount of sales generated by the company.
kpis.description: Revenue represents sales of Inspire systems to hospitals and surgical centers.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting the cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin indicates the direct profitability of Inspire system sales.
kpis.signal: Very high gross margin, sign of high value-added product.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Total profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income shows the company's overall performance after accounting for all charges.

kpis.name: Research and Development Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs incurred for research and development of new products or improvement of existing products.
kpis.description: R&D expenses are critical for future development of Inspire systems and expansion of indications.

kpis.name: Sales and Marketing Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to promotion, sales, and distribution of products.
kpis.description: Sales and marketing expenses aim to educate patients and physicians on the benefits of Inspire therapy.
kpis.signal: Sustained efforts to increase awareness and adoption.

kpis.name: Accumulated Deficit
kpis.explanation: Cumulative net loss since company inception.
kpis.description: Accumulated deficit reflects past losses, but its reduction indicates improvement in overall financial health.
kpis.signal: Reduction in accumulated deficit due to increasing profitability.

kpis.name: U.S. Revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue generated from the U.S. market.
kpis.description: The United States represents 95.6% of Inspire Medical Systems sales in 2025.
kpis.signal: Strong dependence on U.S. market for growth.

kpis.name: International Revenue
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue generated outside the United States.
kpis.description: International revenues (4.4% of total) come from sales in Europe and Japan, with planned expansion in Asia-Pacific.

kpis.name: Inventory Obsolescence Charge
kpis.explanation: Cost of inventory that has become obsolete or expired.
kpis.description: Charge recorded in 2025 for excess components related to the Inspire IV system.
kpis.signal: One-time impact on results from inventory management.

risks.title: Reimbursement uncertainty for Inspire V
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the 10-K, with repeated mentions of current confusion over CPT coding and potential impact on revenues. Language is alarming (confusion, impact on our results). Compared to prior year, risk intensifies with Inspire V launch. Capital category is highly weighted as directly linked to cash flows.

risks.title: Competition from GLP-1 treatments for sleep apnea
risks.score_rationale: The document devotes multiple paragraphs to GLP-1s, citing studies such as SURMOUNT-OSA. Language shows heightened vigilance, though the company believes in a complementary effect. Risk is new in depth since Zepbound approval in 2024. Competition category is critical for target market sustainability.

risks.title: Dependence on single suppliers
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of single-source suppliers and past disruptions. Risk is stable but severe, with direct production impact. Company acknowledges obsolescence risk, as illustrated by 2.1M$ charge in 2025. Industrial category is highly weighted in medical devices.

risks.title: Obsolescence of component inventory
risks.score_rationale: The 10-K cites a 2.1M$ impairment charge in 2025 related to Inspire IV. Language is factual but concerning. Risk is stable, tied to product lifecycle. Capital category reflects direct impact on profitability.

risks.title: Slowing revenue growth
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth rate is moderating from prior years (13.6% YoY in 2025 vs. prior double-digit growth rates implied by history). Market maturation and competitive pressures from GLP-1s could further pressure growth. Capital category is critical as revenues drive profitability.

ai_positioning.summary: The company INSP does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its report. Information provided focuses on financial statements and investments.
